topic: Explain provider, compatible local endpoint and Mycellios network connections without implying universal availability or privacy guarantees.

localizations.title: One project. The right model connection.
localizations.excerpt: A provider, a compatible local endpoint or a network model: understand what each connection changes, what to check and where your project context goes.
localizations.seoTitle: Choose a model connection for your Mico | Mycellios
localizations.seoDescription: Compare provider, compatible local endpoint and network connections for your Mico. Understand model availability, context, access and usage before you start.
localizations.imageAlt: A conceptual computing fabric linking personal devices and servers.
localizations.contentHtml:
A project has a goal, notes and decisions. A model connection supplies the inference used to work on that project. Keeping those two ideas clear makes it easier to choose a suitable setup for your Mico.

Before choosing a model by name, ask what the next task requires. A short outline, a long document review and a task involving tools may need different capabilities. Check the models and connections actually available in your workspace.

Start with the task

Write down the expected input and output. Will you share a few paragraphs or several documents? Do you need text only? Does the task need tools, and are those tools available in your execution environment?

A model that answers a short question successfully has not necessarily demonstrated the context capacity or tool support your larger task needs. Begin with a small, representative request before committing a whole workflow to a connection.

A provider connection

A provider connection sends model requests to the service you configure. Your available models, usage limits and charges depend on that service and the credentials or account used for the connection.

Review its current data terms before sharing project material. The information included in a model request is processed by the selected service; keeping notes in a Mycellios workspace does not make every inference request local.

Check that credentials are configured through the connection settings. Do not paste API keys into a conversation or attach them to project notes.

A compatible local endpoint

A local connection points to a compatible model endpoint you operate. The model service must be running, reachable by the component making the request and configured with the right access controls.

Check the endpoint address, model identifier and available memory. A local address on your computer is not automatically reachable from a runner on another computer or server. Where the request originates matters as much as where the model is hosted.

Also review the rest of the task. A locally hosted model does not make an external tool or connected service local. Consider each destination that receives the information needed for the work.

A Mycellios network connection

A network connection depends on the models, compatible runtime support and capacity available through the configured Mycellios service. A device appearing in network statistics is not a guarantee that it can serve your selected model or accept a task immediately.

Use Stats to explore reported network information, then check availability for the actual model and request. Device discovery, available execution capacity and completed inference are different observations.

Mycellios is being built toward a broader compute network. Treat that direction separately from support verified for a particular model, device and runtime.

Check the context when changing connections

If you change the model used for a project, review the notes and instructions included in the next request. A new model should not be expected to know information that has not been supplied to it.

A short handover note helps: the goal, the decisions already made, the current draft and the next question. It also gives you a clear record of what context you intend to share with the selected connection.

Run a small connection check

  • Confirm the endpoint and model are available to your workspace.
  • Send a short request without private project data.
  • Check that the response and required capabilities match your task.
  • Review access, usage and data handling before adding the full context.

You do not need the perfect setup to make a useful start. You need a working connection that fits the next task. Open Agent, check your connection and try one small request.

sourceNotes.note: Reviewed model/runtime capability boundaries and the distinction between local application behavior and physical inference evidence. No provider prices, benchmarks, universal network availability or automatic context migration are asserted.
